name: Piano tuning and repair
summary: How expats find piano tuners and technicians in Singapore for humidity-related pitch drift, condo move damage, and regulation — including how often to tune in tropical conditions.
body:
Pianos hate Singapore’s humidity swings between air-con and open windows. New arrivals unpack a shipped upright only to hear sour octaves within weeks. Tuners and technicians handle pitch, regulation, voicing, and minor repairs; full rebuilds are a different budget.

## Typical needs
- Post-move tuning after relocation or internal condo shifts
- Seasonal pitch correction (often more frequent than temperate climates)
- Sticky keys, pedal issues, and buzz diagnosis
- Digital/hybrid instrument setup — confirm the tech’s scope
- Pre-exam tuning for ABRSM/Trinity candidates

## Condo logistics
Measure lift pads and stair turns before booking a move; many “tuning” calls are actually damage from poor handling. Ask neighbours about quiet hours before evening tunings.

## How to choose
Prefer technicians who explain pitch targets (A440 vs other) and whether your piano can hold tension after a big pitch raise (may need two visits). Get written quotes for parts. Cheap one-pass tunings on a neglected piano often leave it unstable.

## Practical tip
Hold stable room humidity where practical and avoid parking pianos against exterior walls that sweat. Book tuning 1–2 weeks before exams, not the morning of.
